statement.en: This level is set in Winnipeg. In 1869 Canada took the vast northwest region over from the Hudson's Bay Company. The people living along the Red River were not consulted; Discover Canada calls them the 12,000 Métis of the Red River. Louis Riel answered with an armed uprising and took Fort Garry, the territorial capital.
statement.fr: Ce niveau se déroule à Winnipeg. En 1869, le Canada a repris à la Compagnie de la Baie d'Hudson la vaste région du Nord-Ouest. Les gens qui vivaient le long de la rivière Rouge n'ont pas été consultés; Discover Canada les appelle les 12 000 Métis de la rivière Rouge. Louis Riel a répondu par un soulèvement armé et a pris Fort Garry, la capitale du territoire.

source.quote: the 12,000 Métis of the Red River were not consulted. In response, Louis Riel led an armed uprising and seized Fort Garry, the territorial capital.

verification.evidence: When Canada took over the vast northwest region from the Hudson’s Bay Company in 1869, the 12,000 Métis of the Red River were not consulted. In response, Louis Riel led an armed uprising and seized Fort Garry, the territorial capital.

blurb.en: Across the river is St. Boniface, Winnipeg's French Quarter. It has the largest French-speaking community in Western Canada.
blurb.fr: De l'autre côté de la rivière se trouve Saint-Boniface, le quartier français de Winnipeg. On y trouve la plus grande communauté francophone de l'Ouest canadien.

source.quote: Winnipeg's French Quarter, St. Boniface, has Western Canada's largest Francophone community at 45,000.

verification.evidence: Winnipeg’s French Quarter, St. Boniface, has Western Canada’s largest Francophone community at 45,000.

blurb.en: In Canada the law applies to everyone. Judges, politicians and the police must follow the same law as you.
blurb.fr: Au Canada, la loi s'applique à tout le monde. Les juges, les politiciens et les policiers doivent respecter la même loi que vous.

source.quote: The law in Canada applies to everyone, including judges, politicians and the police.

verification.evidence: Canada is governed by an organized system of laws. These laws are the written rules intended to guide people in our society. They are made by elected representatives. The courts settle disputes and the police enforce the laws. The law in Canada applies to everyone, including judges, politicians and the police.

blurb.en: The maple leaf is the best-known symbol of Canada. Canadian soldiers began wearing it in the 1850s.
blurb.fr: La feuille d'érable est le symbole le plus connu du Canada. Les soldats canadiens ont commencé à la porter dans les années 1850.

source.quote: The maple leaf is Canada’s best-known symbol. Maple leaves were adopted as a symbol by French-Canadians in the 1700s, have appeared on Canadian uniforms and insignia since the 1850s, and are carved into the headstones of our fallen soldiers buried overseas and in Canada.

verification.evidence: The maple leaf is Canada’s best-known symbol. Maple leaves were adopted as a symbol by French-Canadians in the 1700s, have appeared on Canadian uniforms and insignia since the 1850s, and are carved into the headstones of our fallen soldiers buried overseas and in Canada.
